claim: Linkage disequilibrium and disease-associated variants in the non-coding regions make it difficult to distinguish the truly associated genes from the redundantly associated genes for complex diseases.
source: Linkage disequilibrium and disease-associated variants in the non-coding regions make it difficult to distinguish the truly associated genes from the redundantly associated genes for complex diseases.
evidence: This is a statement of a known challenge in the field, drawing from established scientific understanding of GWAS limitations.

claim: eDESE is a new conditional gene-based framework that leverages an improved effective chi-squared statistic to control the type I error rates and remove the redundant associations.
source: In this study, we proposed a new conditional gene-based framework called eDESE that leveraged an improved effective chi-squared statistic to control the type I error rates and remove the redundant associations.
evidence: This is the main methodological contribution of the study, supported by the simulation and real data analyses presented.

claim: Isoform-level eQTLs are more powerful than gene-level eQTLs in association analysis.
source: We further demonstrated that the isoform-level eQTLs could be more powerful than the gene-level eQTLs in the association analysis using a simulation study.
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation study results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE are enriched with neuronal or synaptic signaling-related terms in the Gene Ontology knowledgebase.
source: We then applied eDESE to predict the potential susceptibility genes of schizophrenia and found that the potential susceptibility genes were enriched with many neuronal or synaptic signaling-related terms in the Gene Ontology knowledgebase and antipsychotics-gene interaction terms in the drug-gene interaction database (DGIdb).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Seven potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE are target genes of multiple antipsychotics in DrugBank.
source: More importantly, seven potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE were the target genes of multiple antipsychotics in DrugBank.
evidence: This is supported by database searches and presented in Table 5.

claim: Strategy based on isoform-level eQTLs is an important supplement for strategies based on physical distance and gene-level eQTLs.
source: Comparing the potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE and other benchmark approaches (i.e., MAGMA and S-PrediXcan) implied that strategy based on the isoform-level eQTLs could be an important supplement for the other two strategies (physical distance and gene-level eQTLs).
evidence: This is inferred from comparative analyses of different methods presented in the results.

claim: Most susceptibility SNPs only have small effects on a complex phenotype, making conventional SNP-based association tests underpowered.
source: Because most susceptibility SNPs only have small effects on a complex phenotype, conventional SNP-based association tests are generally underpowered to reveal susceptibility variants after multiple-testing corrections.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge in the field of GWAS.

claim: More than 90% of disease-associated variants are in non-coding regions of the genome.
source: Finally, more than 90% of the disease-associated variants are in non-coding regions of the genome, and many of them are far from the nearest known gene, and it remains a challenge to link genes and a complex phenotype through the non-coding variants (Schaub et al., 2012; Maurano et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Gene-based approaches can reduce multiple-testing burdens by considering the association between a phenotype and all variants within a gene.
source: First, gene-based approaches can reduce the multiple-testing burdens by considering the association between a phenotype and all variants within a gene (Neale and Sham, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published methodology.

claim: MAGMA uses a multiple regression approach to incorporate LD between markers and detect multi-marker effects.
source: For example, MAGMA (Multi-marker Analysis of GenoMic Annotation), one of the most popular gene-based approaches, uses a multiple regression approach to incorporate LD between markers and detect multi-markers effects to perform gene-based analysis (de Leeuw et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the methodology of MAGMA as cited from the literature.

claim: Evaluating gene-phenotype associations at one gene conditioning on other genes can isolate true susceptibility genes from redundant non-susceptibility genes.
source: Second, evaluating the gene-phenotype associations at one gene conditioning on other genes can isolate true susceptibility genes from the redundant non-susceptibility genes (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Variants in non-coding regions are enriched in transcriptional regulatory regions.
source: Third, the observation that variants in the non-coding regions were enriched in the transcriptional regulatory regions implied that these variants might affect the disease risk by altering the genetic regulation of target genes (Gallagher and Chen-Plotkin, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Using eQTLs of potentially phenotype-associated tissues might help identify true susceptibility genes in the tissue context.
source: As many complex diseases manifested themselves in certain tissues, using the eQTLs of potentially phenotype-associated tissues might help identify the true susceptibility genes in the tissue context (Hekselman and Yeger-Lotem, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation and represents a methodological rationale.

claim: S-PrediXcan was developed for imputing the genetically regulated gene expression component based on GWAS summary statistics and transcriptome prediction models.
source: S-PrediXcan was developed for imputing the genetically regulated gene expression component based on GWAS summary statistics and transcriptome prediction models built from the eQTL/splicing QTL dataset of the Genotype Tissue Expression (GTEx) project (Barbeira et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the S-PrediXcan method as cited from the literature.

claim: Little attention has been paid to integrating isoform-level eQTLs with GWAS summary statistics.
source: In contrast to the considerable research focusing on integrating gene-level eQTLs with GWAS summary statistics, little attention has been paid to integrating isoform-level eQTLs with GWAS summary statistics.
evidence: This is an observation about the state of the field based on literature review.

claim: Michael Gandal et al. emphasized the importance of isoform-level gene regulatory mechanisms in defining cell type and disease specificity.
source: Michael Gandal et al. estimated the candidate risk genes of three psychiatric disorders based on GWAS summary statistics and isoform-level expression profiles. They emphasized the importance of isoform-level gene regulatory mechanisms in defining cell type and disease specificity (Gandal et al., 2018), and similar analyses and conclusions were generated for Alzheimer's disease (Fan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The previous ECS was hindered by a potential type I error inflation issue.
source: However, we found that the previous ECS was hindered by a potential type I error inflation issue and further undermined the accuracy of DESE.
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' evaluation of their previous method.

claim: eDESE has two important advantages over DESE: it is built based on a new ECS with controlled type I error, and it expands conditional gene-based association analysis by using gene-level and isoform-level cis-eQTLs associations.
source: eDESE inherited the framework of DESE but had two important advantages over DESE. First, eDESE is built based on a new ECS, with which the type I error could be controlled within a proper level. Second, eDESE expands the conditional gene-based association analysis of DESE by not only using physically nearby SNPs but also using the gene-level and isoform-level cis-eQTLs associations (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the methodological description and Figure 1.

claim: The exponent c = 1.0 led to deflated p-values while c = 2.0 led to inflated p-values in the upper tail of the Q-Q plot.
source: As shown in Figure 2, the c = 1.0 led to deflated p-values while the c = 2.0 led to inflated p-values in the upper tail of the Q-Q plot against the uniform distribution.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: The pattern of p-value deviation was independent of sample sizes, variant number and phenotype distribution.
source: This pattern was independent of sample sizes, variant number and phenotype distribution (for binary or continuous traits) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: The favorable c value that could properly control the type I error rate must be within range 1 and 2.
source: The stable trend determined by the c value also implied that the favorable c, which could properly control the type I error rate, measured by the minimal mean log fold change (MLFC), must be within range 1 and 2.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation results and theoretical derivation.

claim: Theoretical derivation demonstrated that the c value should be within range 1 and 2.
source: Besides, our theoretical derivation also demonstrated that the c value should be within range 1 and 2.
evidence: This is based on mathematical derivation presented in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The favorable c values were approximately independent of trait types, sample sizes and variant number.
source: Again, the favorable c values were approximately independent of trait types, sample sizes and variant number.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 3.

claim: The averaged favorable c value is 1.432.
source: For the sake of simplicity, we proposed to use the averaged favorable c value, 1.432, and integrated it into the improved ECS.
evidence: This is calculated from simulation results.

claim: The conditional p-values of genes without truly causal loci approximately follow the uniform distribution U[0,1], regardless of the variance explained by nearby genes.
source: As shown in Figure 4, in six different scenarios, the conditional p-values of the genes without truly casual loci approximately follow the uniform distribution U[0,1], regardless of the variance explained by its nearby genes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 4.

claim: The distribution of conditional p-value was similar to that produced by the conventional likelihood ratio test for nested linear regression models.
source: Moreover, the distribution of conditional p-value was similar to that produced by the conventional likelihood ratio test for the nested linear regression models.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison in simulation results shown in Figure 4.

claim: Conditional gene-based association analysis based on the improved ECS could produce valid p-values for statistical inference.
source: These results suggested that the conditional gene-based association analysis based on the improved ECS could produce valid p-values for statistical inference.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation results showing proper type I error control.

claim: Unconditional association test based on the improved ECS produced inflated p-values due to indirect associations produced by nearby causal genes in the LD block.
source: In contrast, the unconditional association test based on the improved ECS produced an inflated p-value due to the indirect associations produced by the nearby causal genes in the LD block.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 4.

claim: Conditional gene-based association analysis based on the improved ECS produced smaller p-values than the likelihood ratio test, suggesting higher statistical power.
source: Concerning the statistical power, we found that conditional gene-based association analysis based on the improved ECS produced smaller p-values than the likelihood ratio test (Figure 5), suggesting a higher statistical power of the former.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 5.

claim: The improved ECS does not require individual genotypes, which is an advantage over the likelihood ratio test.
source: Another advantage of conditional gene-based association analysis based on the improved ECS over the likelihood ratio test was that the former did not require individual genotypes.
evidence: This is a methodological characteristic of the approach.

claim: The improved ECS identified 739 significant genes without conditioning on gene-expression profiles in schizophrenia analysis.
source: We found that the improved ECS identified 739 significant genes without conditioning on gene-expression profiles.
evidence: This is a result from applying the method to real schizophrenia GWAS data.

claim: eDESE:dist identified 205 significant genes out of 739 genes by conditioning on gene-level expression profiles.
source: Furthermore, we also found 205 significant genes out of the above 739 genes identified by eDESE:dist based on the improved ECS by conditioning on the gene-level expression profiles (see details in Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is a result from applying the method to real schizophrenia GWAS data.

claim: MAGMA identified 619 significant susceptibility genes for schizophrenia.
source: We identified 619 significant susceptibility genes based on MAGMA.
evidence: This is a result from applying MAGMA to schizophrenia GWAS data.

claim: The significant gene count of MAGMA was about three times larger than that of eDESE:dist.
source: The significant gene count of MAGMA was about three times larger than that of eDESE:dist, which might partly result from the conditional gene-based analysis's advantage of removing the redundantly associated genes.
evidence: This is a comparison of results from two methods applied to the same data.

claim: More than half of the significant susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:dist were also identified by MAGMA.
source: Besides, more than half of the significant susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:dist were also identified by MAGMA (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is shown in the Venn diagram in Figure 6a.

claim: Most GO:BP and GO:CC enrichment terms of the overlapped genes identified by MAGMA and eDESE:dist were neuronal-, dendrite- or synaptic signaling-related terms.
source: Interestingly, we found that most GO:BP and GO:CC enrichment terms of the overlapped genes were neuronal-, dendrite- or synaptic signaling-related terms.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The GO:MF enrichment terms of the overlapped genes were all about signaling transduction.
source: The GO:MF enrichment terms of the overlapped genes were all about signaling transduction (see examples in Figure 6b and details in Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The unique genes identified by eDESE:dist were enriched with three GO:CC terms that were all dendrite-related.
source: We then found that the unique genes identified by eDESE:dist were enriched with three GO:CC terms, that is, dendrite, dendritic tree and distal axon, which were all dendrite-related terms.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: None of the GO enrichment terms for unique genes identified by MAGMA were neuronal-, dendrite-, or synaptic signaling-related.
source: However, although the unique genes identified by MAGMA were enriched with thirty-one GO terms, none of these terms were neuronal-, dendrite-, or synaptic signaling-related terms.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: 67 of the 205 (~32.7%) potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:dist had at least two search hits in PubMed.
source: Moreover, systematic text-mining results in PubMed showed that 67 of the 205 (~32.7%) and 170 of the 619 (~27.5%) potential susceptibility genes had at least two search hits for eDESE:dist and MAGMA, respectively (see details in Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: This is based on systematic text-mining analysis of PubMed.

claim: Type I error rates of simulations are controlled within 0% ~ 0.3% (on average <0.1%) according to the p-value threshold 0.001.
source: As shown in Table 1, our simulations' type I error rates are controlled within 0% ~ 0.3% (on average <0.1%) according to the p-value threshold 0.001 (scenarios 1–3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Table 1.

claim: In scenarios where gene expression cannot affect the phenotype, AllVar is much more powerful than eQTLs.
source: As expected, in scenarios 4–6, where gene expression cannot affect the phenotype (Eg = 0 in Table 1), AllVar is much more powerful than eQTLs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Table 1.

claim: The powers of eQTLs roughly increase with the phenotype variance explained by all variants and gene expression variance explained by all variants.
source: Further, in scenarios 7–12, where gene expression can affect the phenotype, our results suggest that the powers of eQTLs roughly increase with the phenotype variance explained by all variants (Vgp in Table 1) and gene expression variance explained by all variants (Vge in Table 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Table 1.

claim: Association tests based on susceptibility isoforms (IsoeQTL and GeneQTL) are more powerful than those based on gene-level eQTLs in scenarios where gene expression can affect the phenotype.
source: Moreover, in scenarios 7–12, associations test totally based on the susceptibility isoforms (IsoeQTL and GeneQTL in Table 1) are more powerful than those based on the gene-level eQTLs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Table 1.

claim: The power of IsoeQTL is equal to GeneQTL despite IsoeQTL being computed based on fewer susceptibility isoforms.
source: While IsoeQTL is computed based on fewer (i.e. one) susceptibility isoforms than GeneQTL (i.e. three), the power of IsoeQTL is the equal of GeneQTL.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Table 1.

claim: Simulation results revealed that isoform-level eQTLs were more powerful than gene-level eQTLs in association analysis in scenarios where gene expression could affect the phenotype.
source: Thus, our simulation results revealed that isoform-level eQTLs were more powerful than gene-level eQTLs in association analysis in the scenarios that gene expression could affect the phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from simulation results.

claim: All thirteen brain regions were significantly associated with schizophrenia and ranked at the top based on gene-level and isoform-level expression profiles.
source: Therefore, we firstly adopted eDESE:dist to predict the phenotype-associated tissues of schizophrenia and found that all thirteen brain regions were significantly associated with schizophrenia and ranked the top based on the gene-level and isoform-level expression profiles, respectively (see details in Supplementary file 1d).
evidence: This is a result from applying eDESE:dist to schizophrenia data.

claim: Brain was predicted as the schizophrenia-associated tissue based on the gene-level eQTLs of twelve brain regions.
source: Our results showed that the brain (all thirteen brain regions as a whole) was predicted as the schizophrenia-associated tissue based on the gene-level eQTLs of twelve brain regions, respectively (Table 2).
evidence: This is shown in Table 2.

claim: Brain was predicted as schizophrenia-associated tissue only based on the isoform-level eQTLs of five brain regions.
source: However, on the more precise resolution, we found brain was predicted as schizophrenia-associated tissue only based on the isoform-level eQTLs of five brain regions, respectively (Table 2).
evidence: This is shown in Table 2.

claim: Five brain regions were collectively optimized as the potentially phenotype-associated tissues of schizophrenia by eDESE:dist, eDESE:gene, and eDESE:isoform.
source: Thus, the five brain regions were collectively optimized as the potentially phenotype-associated tissues of schizophrenia by eDESE:dist, eDESE:gene, and eDESE:isoform.
evidence: This is a conclusion from integrating results from three models.

claim: Neither Muscle Skeletal nor Skin Sun Exposed Lower Leg was predicted to be significant tissues of schizophrenia using their gene-level and isoform-level eQTLs.
source: The prediction results of Muscle Skeletal and Skin Sun Exposed Lower Leg showed that neither of them was predicted to be significant tissues of schizophrenia by using their gene-level and isoform-level eQTLs (see details in Supplementary file 1e), which demonstrated, at least partly, our assumption.
evidence: This is a result from applying the method to non-brain tissues as a control.

claim: The number of potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:isoform was larger than that of eDESE:gene and S-PrediXcan under the same adjustment filter cutoff.
source: We found the number of potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:isoform was larger than that of eDESE:gene and S-PrediXcan under the same adjustment filter cutoff (Figure 7a, see details in Supplementary file 1fg and h).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7a.

claim: The susceptibility genes exclusively identified by eDESE:isoform were the most among the three models (S-PrediXcan, eDESE:gene, and eDESE:isoform).
source: We further combined the potential susceptibility genes of the five optimized brain regions identified by S-PrediXcan, eDESE:gene and eDESE:isoform, respectively. Still, we found that the susceptibility genes exclusively identified by eDESE:isoform were the most among the three models (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is shown in the Venn diagram in Figure 7b.

claim: 135 genes for S-PrediXcan, 170 genes for eDESE:gene and 247 genes for eDESE:isoform had at least one search hit reporting associations with schizophrenia in PubMed.
source: We found that 135 genes for S-PrediXcan, 170 genes for eDESE:gene and 247 genes for eDESE:isoform had at least one search hit which reported the associations of these genes with schizophrenia in PubMed database, respectively (see details in Supplementary file 1ij and k).
evidence: This is based on systematic text-mining analysis of PubMed.

claim: 138 of the 524 (26.3%) potential susceptibility genes exclusively predicted by eDESE:isoform each had at least one search hit in PubMed.
source: We also found 138 of the 524 (26.3%) potential susceptibility genes exclusively predicted by eDESE:isoform each had a least one search hit.
evidence: This is based on systematic text-mining analysis of PubMed.

claim: 19 of the 524 (3.6%) potential susceptibility genes exclusively predicted by eDESE:isoform each had at least 10 supported papers in PubMed.
source: Moreover, we found that 19 of the 524 (3.6%) potential susceptibility genes each had at least 10 supported papers in PubMed (Table 3, see details in ).
evidence: This is based on systematic text-mining analysis of PubMed and shown in Table 3.

claim: TCF4, RGS4 and RANGAP1 were reported by more than 100 papers in PubMed.
source: Interestingly, TCF4 (transcription factor 4), RGS4 (regulator of G protein signaling 4) and RANGAP1 (Ran GTPase activating protein 1) were reported by more than 100 papers.
evidence: This is based on text-mining analysis of PubMed.

claim: RGS4 is reported to be biased expressed in brain.
source: RGS4 is reported to be biased expressed in brain (O'Leary et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: TCF4 and RANGAP1 are broadly expressed in the brain, and TCF4 may play an important role in nervous system development.
source: TCF4 and RANGAP1 are broadly expressed in the brain, and TCF4 may play an important role in nervous system development (O'Leary et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: RGS4 and RANGAP1 both had multiple significant meta path types indicating their potential associations and mechanisms associated with schizophrenia in Hetionet.
source: We found that RGS4 and RANGAP1 both had multiple significant meta path types indicating their potential associations and mechanisms associated with schizophrenia.
evidence: This is based on analysis using the Hetionet database.

claim: The potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE guided by eQTLs had more biologically sensible GO enrichment terms than S-PrediXcan.
source: Next, we performed the GO enrichment analysis and found that the potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE guided by the eQTLs (eDESE:gene and eDESE:isoform) had more biologically sensible GO enrichment terms than S-PrediXcan (Table 4).
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results shown in Table 4.

claim: The potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:isoform were enriched with more neuronal, dendritic or synaptic signaling-related biological process GO terms than S-PrediXcan and eDESE:gene.
source: In addition, the GO enrichment results also showed that the potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:isoform were enriched with more neuronal, dendritic or synaptic signaling-related biological process GO terms than S-PrediXcan and eDESE:gene.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The 55 genes commonly identified by S-PrediXcan, eDESE:gene and eDESE:isoform were enriched with no GO term.
source: However, we found that the 55 genes commonly identified by the three models were enriched with no GO term.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The 240 unique genes identified by S-PrediXcan were enriched with no GO term.
source: Furthermore, the 240 unique genes identified by S-PrediXcan were also enriched with no GO term.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The 319 unique genes identified by eDESE:gene were enriched with 'integral component of synaptic vesicle membrane' (CC) and several general GO terms.
source: On the other hand, the 319 unique genes identified by the eDESE:gene were enriched with 'integral component of synaptic vesicle membrane' (CC) and several general GO terms.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The 524 unique genes identified by eDESE:isoform were enriched with a considerable number of GO terms, including neuronal, dendritic or synaptic signaling-related GO terms.
source: In comparison, the 524 unique genes identified by eDESE:isoform were enriched with a considerable number of GO terms, in which a few neuronal, dendritic or synaptic signaling-related GO terms were found (Supplementary file 1l).
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: The potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:gene and eDESE:isoform based on Brain-Cerebellum eQTLs were both enriched with a brain consensus module (colored 'turquoise') with statistical significance.
source: We found that the potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:gene and eDESE:isoform based on the gene-level and isoform-level eQTLs of Brain-Cerebellum were both enriched with a brain consensus module (colored 'turquoise') with statistical significance, that is, adjusted p-value = 0.0046 and 0.0061, respectively.
evidence: This is based on weighted gene co-expression network analysis.

claim: The potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:gene based on Brain-Frontal Cortex (BA9) gene-level eQTLs were enriched with the consensus module colored 'turquoise' (adjusted p-value = 0.024).
source: Besides, the potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:gene based on the gene-level eQTLs of Brain-Frontal Cortex (BA9) were also enriched (adjusted p-value = 0.024) with the consensus module colored 'turquoise'.
evidence: This is based on weighted gene co-expression network analysis.

claim: No enriched consensus module was found for the potential susceptibility genes identified by S-PrediXcan.
source: However, no enriched consensus module was found for the potential susceptibility genes identified by S-PrediXcan.
evidence: This is based on weighted gene co-expression network analysis.

claim: The 'turquoise' consensus module contained 7,726 genes and was enriched with plenty of neuronal and synaptic signaling-related GO terms.
source: Moreover, we found that the 'turquoise' consensus module contained 7,726 genes and was enriched with plenty of neuronal and synaptic signaling-related GO terms (Figure 8, see details in Supplementary file 1m).
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis of the consensus module, shown in Figure 8.

claim: The number or type of susceptibility isoforms for a gene varied greatly in different optimized brain regions.
source: Interestingly, we found that the number or type of susceptibility isoforms for a gene varied greatly in the different optimized brain regions.
evidence: This is based on analysis of isoform-level results from eDESE:isoform.

claim: NAGA and CHRNA2 were reported to be associated with schizophrenia by three and seven research papers in PubMed, respectively.
source: For example, NAGA and CHRNA2 were reported to be associated with schizophrenia by three and seven research papers in the PubMed database, respectively.
evidence: This is based on text-mining analysis of PubMed.

claim: ENST00000407991 of CHRNA2 was significantly associated with schizophrenia only in Brain-Cerebellum.
source: ENST00000407991 of CHRNA2 was significantly associated with schizophrenia only in Brain-Cerebellum, while ENST00000396398 of NAGA was significantly associated with schizophrenia in all the five optimized brain regions.
evidence: This is based on isoform-level analysis results from eDESE:isoform.

claim: Different isoforms of SNX19 were predicted to be significantly associated with schizophrenia in different optimized brain regions.
source: For example, SNX19 was reported to be associated with schizophrenia by seven research papers. ENST00000527116 of SNX19 in Brain-Anterior cingulate cortex (BA24), ENST00000528555 of SNX19 in Brain-Cerebellum, ENST00000265909 of SNX19 in Brain-Frontal Cortex (BA9) and Brain-Hippocampus, and ENST00000526579 of SNX19 in Brain-Spinal cord (cervical c-1) were significantly associated with schizophrenia, respectively.
evidence: This is based on isoform-level analysis results from eDESE:isoform.

claim: Seven potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE in total were the target genes of multiple antipsychotics.
source: Since drug target genes with genetic support are twice or as likely to be approved than target genes with no known genetic associations (King et al., 2019; Nelson et al., 2015), we searched the DrugBank database (Wishart et al., 2018) and found that seven potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE in total (0.976% for eDESE:dist, 0.632% for eDESE:gene and 0.703% for eDESE:isoform) were the target genes of multiple antipsychotics (Table 5).
evidence: This is based on database searches in DrugBank, shown in Table 5.

claim: Three genes (0.485%) of the 619 potential susceptibility genes identified by MAGMA were the target genes of multiple antipsychotics.
source: Besides, we found that three genes (0.485%) of the 619 potential susceptibility genes identified by MAGMA were also the target genes of multiple antipsychotics.
evidence: This is based on database searches in DrugBank.

claim: One gene (0.256%) of the 391 potential susceptibility genes identified by S-PrediXcan was the target gene of an atypical antipsychotic (paliperidone).
source: One gene (0.256%) of the 391 potential susceptibility genes identified by S-PrediXcan was the target gene of an atypical antipsychotic (i.e. paliperidone).
evidence: This is based on database searches in DrugBank.

claim: 'Antipsychotic' - 'potential susceptibility gene' interaction terms identified by MAGMA and the three models of eDESE were all significantly enriched in DGIdb.
source: As shown in Table 6, we found that 'antipsychotic' - 'potential susceptibility gene' interaction terms identified by MAGMA and the three models of eDESE were all significantly enriched in DGIdb.
evidence: This is based on hypergeometric distribution test results shown in Table 6.

claim: Only 12 'antipsychotic'- 'potential susceptibility gene' interaction terms were found for S-PrediXcan (hypergeometric distribution test p-value = 0.33).
source: We also found 452 drug-gene interaction terms for the susceptibility gene identified by S-PrediXcan. However, only 12 'antipsychotic'- 'potential susceptibility gene' interaction terms were found (hypergeometric distribution test p-value = 0.33).
evidence: This is based on database searches in DGIdb and statistical testing.

claim: The top potentially druggable category for potential susceptibility genes identified by MAGMA, S-PrediXcan and eDESE was the 'DRUGGABLE GENOME'.
source: Among the 42 potentially druggable gene categories in DGIdb, we found that the top potentially druggable category for the potential susceptibility genes identified by MAGMA, S-PrediXcan and eDESE all were the "DRUGGABLE GENOME".
evidence: This is based on analysis of druggable gene categories in DGIdb.

claim: The number of 'DRUGGABLE GENOME' genes were 168 (27.1%) for MAGMA, 86 (22.0%) for S-PrediXcan, 62 (30.2%) for eDESE:dist, 136 (21.5%) for eDESE:gene and 207 (24.2%) for eDESE:isoform.
source: The number of "DRUGGABLE GENOME" genes were 168 (27.1%) for MAGMA, 86 (22.0%) for S-PrediXcan, 62 (30.2%) for eDESE:dist, 136 (21.5%) for eDESE:gene and 207 (24.2%) for eDESE:isoform.
evidence: This is based on analysis of druggable gene categories in DGIdb.

claim: Conditional association test based on the new ECS showed a lower type I error rate and higher statistical power compared with the unconditional association test and likelihood ratio test.
source: Compared with the unconditional association test based on the new ECS and likelihood ratio test, the conditional association test based on the new ECS showed a lower type I error rate and higher statistical power.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on simulation results.

claim: eDESE:dist predicted a smaller size of potential susceptibility genes than MAGMA, but more than half of the genes identified by eDESE:dist were also identified by MAGMA.
source: Although eDESE:dist predicted a smaller size of potential susceptibility genes than MAGMA, more than half of the genes identified by eDESE:dist were also identified by MAGMA.
evidence: This is based on comparison of results from the two methods.

claim: The overlapped potential susceptibility genes (accounting for 51.2% in eDESE:dist and 17.0% in MAGMA) were enriched with plenty of neuronal- or synaptic signaling-related GO terms.
source: The overlapped potential susceptibility genes (accounting for 51.2% in eDESE:dist and 17.0% in MAGMA) were enriched with plenty of neuronal- or synaptic signaling-related GO terms.
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: Four of the five optimized brain regions were also reported by the Schizophrenia Working Group of the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium.
source: Interestingly, four of the five optimized brain regions (i.e. Brain-Anterior cingulate cortex (BA24), Brain-Cerebellum, Brain-Frontal Cortex (BA9), and Brain-Hippocampus) were also reported by the Schizophrenia Working Group of the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, in which the genes with high relative specificity for bulk expression were strongly enriched with schizophrenia associations (Trubetskoy et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: eDESE:isoform could identify more susceptibility genes supported by published papers and enriched with biologically sensible GO biological process terms compared to eDESE:gene and S-PrediXcan.
source: We found that eDESE:isoform could identify more susceptibility genes supported by the published papers and enriched with biologically sensible GO biological process terms.
evidence: This is based on comparative analysis of results from the three methods.

claim: Six (85.7%) of the seven target genes of FDA-approved antipsychotics were found by eDESE:isoform.
source: Seven susceptibility genes identified by eDESE were found to be the target genes of multiple FDA-approved antipsychotics, and six (85.7%) of the seven target genes were found by eDESE:isoform.
evidence: This is based on database searches and comparison of results.

claim: The number of potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:isoform and denoted as 'DRUGGABLE GENOME' in DGIdb were the most among MAGMA, S-PrediXcan, and eDESE.
source: Moreover, we found that the number of potential susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:isoform and denoted as 'DRUGGABLE GENOME' in DGIdb, were the most among MAGMA, S-PrediXcan, and eDESE.
evidence: This is based on analysis of druggable gene categories.

claim: The moderate sample size in GTEx (v8) might lead the gene/isoform-level eQTLs to be underpowered.
source: First, the moderate sample size in GTEx (v8) might lead the gene/isoform-level eQTLs to be underpowered.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors.

claim: The size of the susceptibility genes identified by eDESE:gene and eDESE:isoform was a little larger than that of conventional studies.
source: Second, the size of the susceptibility genes identified by the eDESE:gene and eDESE:isoform was a little larger than that of the conventional studies.
evidence: This is an observation about the results.

claim: Gene-level and isoform-level eQTLs were selected based on a lenient threshold (p-value < 0.01) to involve more eQTLs in the association analysis.
source: The main reasons might lie in the gene-level and isoform-level eQTLs selected based on a lenient threshold (p-value < 0.01) to involve more eQTLs in the association analysis, which was taken as the remedy against the underpowered eQTLs.
evidence: This is a methodological choice explained by the authors.

claim: The performance of conditional association analysis for fine-mapping can be greatly influenced by the gene orders of entering the analysis.
source: Third, the performance of conditional association analysis for fine-mapping can be greatly influenced by the gene orders of entering the analysis.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors.

claim: The optimal c value of the effective chi-squared test is still empirical although its range and relevant factors were derived.
source: Fourth, the optimal c value of the effective chi-squared test is still empirical although we derived its range and relevant factors.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors.

claim: The application of the framework to schizophrenia revealed many novel susceptible and druggable candidate genes.
source: The application of our framework to schizophrenia revealed many novel susceptible and druggable candidate genes.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the real data application results.

claim: The usage of isoform-level eQTLs can be an important supplement for conventional gene-based approaches.
source: Besides, our results suggested that the usage of isoform-level eQTLs can be an important supplement for the conventional gene-based approaches.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparative analyses.

claim: Gene-level expression profiles may omit the expression heterogeneity among isoforms, neutralize opposite effects, and lower the power of gene-level eQTLs.
source: Thus, gene-level expression profiles may omit the expression heterogeneity among these isoforms, neutralize the opposite effects, and lower the power of gene-level eQTLs.
evidence: This is a theoretical rationale for why isoform-level eQTLs might be more powerful.

claim: The correlation of chi-squared statistics between two loci was approximated by the absolute value of genotypic correlation to the power of c.
source: The correlation of chi-squared statistics between two loci was approximated by the absolute value of genotypic correlation to the power of c, that is, |r|c.
evidence: This is a methodological detail of the ECS approach.

claim: Exponent c ranged from 1 to 2, corresponding to different noncentrality parameters of a non-central chi-squared distribution.
source: We derived that exponent c ranged from 1 to 2, corresponding to different noncentrality parameters of a non-central chi-squared distribution (See the derivation in the third section of Materials and methods).
evidence: This is based on theoretical derivation presented in the manuscript.

claim: The correlation between two non-central chi-square variables converges to |r| as the noncentrality parameter approaches infinity.
source: Therefore, the correlation of X2 and Y2 converges to |r| as λ→∞
evidence: This is based on mathematical derivation.

claim: The schizophrenia GWAS included 53,386 cases and 77,258 controls of European ancestry samples.
source: The schizophrenia GWAS included 53,386 cases and 77,258 controls of European ancestry samples (hg19 assembly).
evidence: This describes the data used in the study.

claim: Variants in the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region were excluded in the present study because of high polymorphism.
source: The variants in the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region, i.e., chr6:27,477,797–34,448,354, were excluded in the present study because of the high polymorphism.
evidence: This is a methodological choice explained by the authors.
